office_does: The county assessor sets the market value of every taxable property each year and applies property-tax exemptions; taxing districts, not the assessor, decide how much tax is collected.
race_blurb: Two Republicans: incumbent Jacob Tate, a 30-year veteran of the office seeking a second term, faces first-time candidate Keith Effler, a photographer and developer endorsed by the county Republican Party. Tate stresses accurate, equitable appraisal and modernization; Effler pledges customer service, an online valuation data portal and cutting the tax burden as far as the law allows.

candidates.summary: Incumbent assessor with more than 30 years in the office, including as chief deputy under two predecessors, holding the IAAO Mass Appraisal Specialist designation.
highlights: More than 30 years in the assessor's office; assessor since 2022 [S1][S2]
Says the office shrank from 34 employees to 24 positions through modernization [S2]
Says the assessor's job is accurate, equitable values, not raising or lowering taxes [S2]
Plans online exemption applications for seniors and people with disabilities [S2]

experience.basis: Incumbent assessor with more than 30 years in the office, including as chief deputy.

spending.basis: Cites cutting the office from 34 employees to 24 positions and doing more with fewer people through modernization.

candidates.summary: Commercial photographer, developer and Republican precinct committee officer making a first run for office on a taxpayer-first, customer-service platform.
highlights: Pledges to cut the tax burden 'as far as the law allows' and make the county 'the cheapest tax base in Washington' [S1]
Would launch an online 'data-depot' explaining valuations, comparable sales and parcel tax coefficients [S2][S3]
Would put all forms, including senior exemption forms, online [S2][S4]
Endorsed by the Yakima County Republican Party [S1][S2]

experience.basis: First run for county office from a business background, against a 30-year office veteran; says he won't befriend state officials.

taxes.basis: Statement pledges to 'only collect an absolute minimum,' cut the tax burden as far as the law allows and make the county the cheapest tax base in the state.
